what_happened: On a multi-lane highway, the policy steered the ego left toward the next lane, even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. Its front hit actor 41, a pickup passing in that left lane, while the recorded human path stayed in the original lane to the right.

After the policy took over at 4.6 s on a straight highway, the ego slowed hard for no reason (17 to 9 m/s with a clear, widening gap ahead) and drifted left out of its lane toward the recorded path. Its front hit actor 1, which was overtaking in the left lane; something also hit the ego's rear after it braked.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego's own planned path bent left even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. The ego drifted left across the lane line into the next lane while actor 41 was passing it there, and its front clipped 41's rear at about 4 m/s.

On a multi-lane highway, the policy's planned path (orange) swung left toward the adjacent left lane while the ego slowed from 5.7 to 4.2 m/s. Actor 41, a pickup, was coming up alongside in that lane, and the ego drifted into it, hitting it with its front at 7.2 s. The command was STRAIGHT until the last frame, when it became RIGHT, and the human-driven route stayed in the ego's own lane.

On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT command, the policy took over at 4.6s, braked from about 16 to 8 m/s and steered left toward the adjacent lane, while the recorded human path stayed straight and slightly right. The ego's front hit actor 1, which was in that left lane just ahead (the gap dropped to 3.6 m). The ego was also rear-ended at some point; that is likely linked to the hard braking, but the frames don't show when.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the policy took over at 4.6 s, braked hard for no clear reason (17 down to 8 m/s, with the lead car 18 still about 20 m ahead) and steered left toward the next lane. The braking let car 1 in that lane come up level with the ego, and the ego's front corner hit it. The rear contact (`rear_ended`) is likely a car behind hitting the ego because of the sudden slowdown.

On a multi-lane freeway, the policy slowed from 6.8 to 4.5 m/s and steered left toward the next lane, off the recorded straight path. Vehicle 41 was passing on the left, and the ego's front hit it as the ego crossed the lane line.

After the policy took over at 4.6s on the highway, the ego braked hard (from 20 to 11.5 m/s) and drifted left of the recorded path, about 2.3 m from where the human was. At 6.1s its left side hit actor 1, which was driving alongside in the left lane, even though the route command was RIGHT. The hard braking also let a following vehicle rear-end the ego, but the lateral contact counts as the at-fault collision.

With the route command RIGHT and the route path heading right, the policy instead held its own planned path along the left edge of the leftmost lane and drifted over the yellow left-edge line toward the guardrail and median. It slowed from about 20 to 16 m/s and went off-road at 10.3 s, 1.6 m left of the recorded human path, with no actors nearby.

The route command was RIGHT and the route (green line) bore right, but the policy's planned path (orange) kept drifting left. The ego crossed the yellow centre line toward the opposing side and the guardrail, and at 11.1 s, going about 14 m/s, it was counted as off the road. No vehicle was ahead, and the camera view stayed usable, so the policy's own steering caused this.

On a multi-lane freeway, the route was straight and then RIGHT, but after handoff the ego steered steadily left across lanes, about 4.9 m off the recorded path. It ran front-first into vehicle 28 in the lane to its left at about 7.4 m/s.

The route command switched from STRAIGHT to RIGHT, but the ego kept drifting left at about 7 m/s, moving away from the recorded path (4.8 m off by the end). It changed lanes into the lane to its left and hit vehicle 28 with its front at 7.6 s. Vehicle 28 had been coming up behind and to the left of the ego and was alongside, overlapping the ego's front, at impact.

On the highway, the ego was in the leftmost lane, and the route command was RIGHT. Instead of following the recorded path to the right, it planned and steered left at about 4.5–4.8 m/s and drifted onto the left shoulder by the concrete median barrier. It went offroad about 3.7 m from where the human drove, with no traffic forcing it there and a clear camera view before the failure.

The route said RIGHT and the recorded human moved right, but the policy drifted left into the next lane at about 7.4 m/s. A faster car (actor 28) was coming up and passing in that lane, and the ego's front hit it at about 7.5 s, 4.7 m off the human's path.

On a congested multi-lane highway, at about 4 m/s with the route command RIGHT, the ego drifted left, away from the recorded path. It followed its own leftward-curving plan toward the median barrier and was offroad at 9.0 s, 3.7 m off the human trajectory. No actor was close, and the smearing on the barrier in the camera view looks like a result of the drift, not the cause.

On a multi-lane highway with a RIGHT command, the policy planned and drove a path veering left out of its lane, away from the recorded trajectory (3.7 m off), and ended up on the left concrete median barrier edge at about 4.9 m/s, where it was flagged offroad. The camera view was coherent before the drift, so it does not explain the leftward steering.

On a divided highway with a RIGHT command, the ego slowed from about 19 to 15 m/s but kept tracking straight and slightly left. Meanwhile the recorded path curved right. The ego crossed the yellow left edge line onto the shoulder beside the guardrail and was flagged offroad about 1.6 m from the human trajectory. No other actor was involved, and the camera view stayed clear enough to show the lane before the failure.

The route command was RIGHT and the planned path curved right toward the exit, but the ego kept drifting left at about 15 m/s. It crossed the yellow left edge line onto the left shoulder next to the guardrail and was offroad at 11.8 s. At that moment actor 91, coming up from behind on the right, made contact with the ego (it was flagged as a rear contact, not an at-fault collision), but the failure is the ego leaving the road.
